{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Base directory for this skill: /Users/liana/Documents/prog/buidl-guidl/ethskills-evals/artifacts/testing-quiz-004/2026-07-27T081134Z-claude-with-skill-2/workspace/.claude/skills/testing\n\n# Smart Contract Testing\n\n## What You Probably Got Wrong\n\n**You test getters and trivial functions.** Testing that `name()` returns the name is worthless. Test edge cases, failure modes, and economic invariants — the things that lose money when they break.\n\n**You don't fuzz.** `forge test` finds the bugs you thought of. Fuzzing finds the ones you didn't. If your contract does math, fuzz it. If it handles user input, fuzz it. If it moves value, definitely fuzz it.\n\n**You don't fork-test.** If your contract calls Uniswap, Aave, or any external protocol (verified addresses: `addresses/SKILL.md`), test against their real deployed contracts on a fork. Mocking them hides integration bugs that only appear with real state.\n\n**You write tests that mirror the implementation.** Testing that `deposit(100)` sets `balance[user] = 100` is tautological — you're testing that Solidity assignments work. Test properties: \"after deposit and withdraw, user gets their tokens back.\" Test invariants: \"total deposits always equals contract balance.\"\n\n**You skip invariant testing for stateful protocols.** If your contract has multiple interacting functions that change state over time (vaults, AMMs, lending), you need invariant tests. Unit tests check one path; invariant tests check that properties hold across thousands of random sequences.\n\n---\n\n## Unit Testing with Foundry\n\n### Test File Structure\n\n```solidity\n// test/MyContract.t.sol\n// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT\npragma solidity ^0.8.20;\n\nimport {Test, console} from \"forge-std/Test.sol\";\nimport {MyToken} from \"../src/MyToken.sol\";\n\ncontract MyTokenTest is Test {\n    MyToken public token;\n    address public alice = makeAddr(\"alice\");\n    address public bob = makeAddr(\"bob\");\n\n    function setUp() public {\n        token = new MyToken(\"Test\", \"TST\", 1_000_000e18);\n        // Give alice some tokens for testing\n        token.transfer(alice, 10_000e18);\n    }\n\n    function test_TransferUpdatesBalances() public {\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        token.transfer(bob, 1_000e18);\n\n        assertEq(token.balanceOf(alice), 9_000e18);\n        assertEq(token.balanceOf(bob), 1_000e18);\n    }\n\n    function test_TransferEmitsEvent() public {\n        vm.expectEmit(true, true, false, true);\n        emit Transfer(alice, bob, 500e18);\n\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        token.transfer(bob, 500e18);\n    }\n\n    function test_RevertWhen_TransferExceedsBalance() public {\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        vm.expectRevert();\n        token.transfer(bob, 999_999e18); // More than alice has\n    }\n\n    function test_RevertWhen_TransferToZeroAddress() public {\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        vm.expectRevert();\n        token.transfer(address(0), 100e18);\n    }\n}\n```\n\n### Key Assertion Patterns\n\n```solidity\n// Equality\nassertEq(actual, expected);\nassertEq(actual, expected, \"descriptive error message\");\n\n// Comparisons\nassertGt(a, b);   // a > b\nassertGe(a, b);   // a >= b\nassertLt(a, b);   // a < b\nassertLe(a, b);   // a <= b\n\n// Approximate equality (for math with rounding)\nassertApproxEqAbs(actual, expected, maxDelta);\nassertApproxEqRel(actual, expected, maxPercentDelta); // in WAD (1e18 = 100%)\n\n// Revert expectations\nvm.expectRevert();                           // Any revert\nvm.expectRevert(\"Insufficient balance\");     // Specific message\nvm.expectRevert(MyContract.CustomError.selector); // Custom error\n\n// Event expectations\nvm.expectEmit(true, true, false, true);      // (topic1, topic2, topic3, data)\nemit MyEvent(expectedArg1, expectedArg2);\n```\n\n### What to Actually Test\n\n```solidity\n// ✅ TEST: Edge cases that lose money\nfunction test_TransferZeroAmount() public { /* ... */ }\nfunction test_TransferEntireBalance() public { /* ... */ }\nfunction test_TransferToSelf() public { /* ... */ }\nfunction test_ApproveOverwrite() public { /* ... */ }\nfunction test_TransferFromWithExactAllowance() public { /* ... */ }\n\n// ✅ TEST: Access control\nfunction test_RevertWhen_NonOwnerCallsAdminFunction() public { /* ... */ }\nfunction test_OwnerCanPause() public { /* ... */ }\n\n// ✅ TEST: Failure modes\nfunction test_RevertWhen_DepositZero() public { /* ... */ }\nfunction test_RevertWhen_WithdrawMoreThanDeposited() public { /* ... */ }\nfunction test_RevertWhen_ContractPaused() public { /* ... */ }\n\n// ❌ DON'T TEST: OpenZeppelin internals\n// function test_NameReturnsName() — they already tested this\n// function test_SymbolReturnsSymbol() — waste of time\n// function test_DecimalsReturns18() — it does, trust it\n```\n\n---\n\n## Fuzz Testing\n\nFoundry automatically fuzzes any test function with parameters. Instead of testing one value, it tests hundreds of random values.\n\n### Basic Fuzz Test\n\n```solidity\n// Foundry calls this with random amounts\nfunction testFuzz_DepositWithdrawRoundtrip(uint256 amount) public {\n    // Bound input to valid range\n    amount = bound(amount, 1, token.balanceOf(alice));\n\n    uint256 balanceBefore = token.balanceOf(alice);\n\n    vm.startPrank(alice);\n    token.approve(address(vault), amount);\n    vault.deposit(amount, alice);\n    vault.withdraw(vault.balanceOf(alice), alice, alice);\n    vm.stopPrank();\n\n    // Property: user gets back what they deposited (minus any fees)\n    assertGe(token.balanceOf(alice), balanceBefore - 1); // Allow 1 wei rounding\n}\n```\n\n### Bounding Inputs\n\n```solidity\n// bound() is preferred over vm.assume() — bound reshapes, assume discards\nfunction testFuzz_Fee(uint256 amount, uint256 feeBps) public {\n    amount = bound(amount, 1e6, 1e30);       // Reasonable token amounts\n    feeBps = bound(feeBps, 1, 10_000);       // 0.01% to 100%\n\n    uint256 fee = (amount * feeBps) / 10_000;\n    uint256 afterFee = amount - fee;\n\n    // Property: fee + remainder always equals original\n    assertEq(fee + afterFee, amount);\n}\n\n// vm.assume() discards inputs — use sparingly\nfunction testFuzz_Division(uint256 a, uint256 b) public {\n    vm.assume(b > 0); // Skip zero (would revert)\n    // ...\n}\n```\n\n### Run with More Iterations\n\n```bash\n# Default: 256 runs\nforge test\n\n# More thorough: 10,000 runs\nforge test --fuzz-runs 10000\n\n# Set in foundry.toml for CI\n# [fuzz]\n# runs = 1000\n```\n\n---\n\n## Fork Testing\n\nTest your contract against real deployed protocols on a mainnet fork. This catches integration bugs that mocks can't.\n\n### Basic Fork Test\n\n```solidity\ncontract SwapTest is Test {\n    // Real mainnet addresses — full verified list: addresses/SKILL.md\n    address constant UNISWAP_ROUTER = 0x68b3465833fb72A70ecDF485E0e4C7bD8665Fc45;\n    address constant WETH = 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2;\n    address constant USDC = 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48;\n\n    function setUp() public {\n        // Fork mainnet at a specific block for reproducibility\n        vm.createSelectFork(\"mainnet\", 19_000_000);\n    }\n\n    function test_SwapETHForUSDC() public {\n        address user = makeAddr(\"user\");\n        vm.deal(user, 1 ether);\n\n        vm.startPrank(user);\n\n        // Build swap path\n        ISwapRouter.ExactInputSingleParams memory params = ISwapRouter\n            .ExactInputSingleParams({\n                tokenIn: WETH,\n                tokenOut: USDC,\n                fee: 3000,\n                recipient: user,\n                amountIn: 0.1 ether,\n                amountOutMinimum: 0, // In production, NEVER set to 0\n                sqrtPriceLimitX96: 0\n            });\n\n        // Execute swap\n        uint256 amountOut = ISwapRouter(UNISWAP_ROUTER).exactInputSingle{value: 0.1 ether}(params);\n\n        vm.stopPrank();\n\n        // Verify we got USDC back\n        assertGt(amountOut, 0, \"Should receive USDC\");\n        assertGt(IERC20(USDC).balanceOf(user), 0);\n    }\n}\n```\n\n### When to Fork-Test\n\n- **Always:** Any contract that calls an external protocol (Uniswap, Aave, Chainlink)\n- **Always:** Any contract that handles tokens with quirks (USDT, fee-on-transfer, rebasing)\n- **Always:** Any contract that reads oracle prices\n- **Never:** Pure logic contracts with no external calls — use unit tests\n\n### Running Fork Tests\n\n```bash\n# Fork from RPC URL\nforge test --fork-url https://eth-mainnet.g.alchemy.com/v2/YOUR_KEY\n\n# Fork at specific block (reproducible)\nforge test --fork-url https://eth-mainnet.g.alchemy.com/v2/YOUR_KEY --fork-block-number 19000000\n\n# Set in foundry.toml to avoid CLI flags\n# [rpc_endpoints]\n# mainnet = \"${MAINNET_RPC_URL}\"\n```\n\n---\n\n## Invariant Testing\n\nInvariant tests verify that properties hold across thousands of random function call sequences. Essential for stateful protocols.\n\n### What Are Invariants?\n\nInvariants are properties that must ALWAYS be true, no matter what sequence of actions users take:\n\n- \"Total supply equals sum of all balances\" (ERC-20)\n- \"Total deposits equals total shares times share price\" (vault)\n- \"x * y >= k after every swap\" (AMM)\n- \"User can always withdraw what they deposited\" (escrow)\n\n### Basic Invariant Test\n\n```solidity\ncontract VaultInvariantTest is Test {\n    MyVault public vault;\n    IERC20 public token;\n    VaultHandler public handler;\n\n    function setUp() public {\n        token = new MockERC20(\"Test\", \"TST\", 18);\n        vault = new MyVault(token);\n        handler = new VaultHandler(vault, token);\n\n        // Tell Foundry which contract to call randomly\n        targetContract(address(handler));\n    }\n\n    // This runs after every random sequence\n    function invariant_TotalAssetsMatchesBalance() public view {\n        assertEq(\n            vault.totalAssets(),\n            token.balanceOf(address(vault)),\n            \"Total assets must equal actual balance\"\n        );\n    }\n\n    function invariant_SharePriceNeverZero() public view {\n        if (vault.totalSupply() > 0) {\n            assertGt(vault.convertToAssets(1e18), 0, \"Share price must never be zero\");\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// Handler: guided random actions\ncontract VaultHandler is Test {\n    MyVault public vault;\n    IERC20 public token;\n\n    constructor(MyVault _vault, IERC20 _token) {\n        vault = _vault;\n        token = _token;\n    }\n\n    function deposit(uint256 amount) public {\n        amount = bound(amount, 1, 1e24);\n        deal(address(token), msg.sender, amount);\n\n        vm.startPrank(msg.sender);\n        token.approve(address(vault), amount);\n        vault.deposit(amount, msg.sender);\n        vm.stopPrank();\n    }\n\n    function withdraw(uint256 shares) public {\n        uint256 maxShares = vault.balanceOf(msg.sender);\n        if (maxShares == 0) return;\n        shares = bound(shares, 1, maxShares);\n\n        vm.prank(msg.sender);\n        vault.redeem(shares, msg.sender, msg.sender);\n    }\n}\n```\n\n### Running Invariant Tests\n\n```bash\n# Default depth (15 calls per sequence, 256 sequences)\nforge test\n\n# Deeper exploration\nforge test --fuzz-runs 1000\n\n# Configure in foundry.toml\n# [invariant]\n# runs = 512\n# depth = 50\n```\n\n---\n\n## What NOT to Test\n\n- **OpenZeppelin internals.** Don't test that `ERC20.transfer` works. It's been audited by dozens of firms and used by thousands of contracts. Test YOUR logic on top of it.\n- **Solidity language features.** Don't test that `require` reverts or that `mapping` stores values. The compiler works.\n- **Every getter.** If `name()` returns the name you passed to the constructor, that's not a test — it's a tautology.\n- **Happy path only.** The happy path probably works. Test the unhappy paths: what happens with zero? Max uint? Unauthorized callers? Reentrancy?\n\n**Focus your testing effort on:** Custom business logic, mathematical operations, integration points with external protocols, access control boundaries, and economic edge cases.\n\n---\n\n## Pre-Deploy Test Checklist\n\n- [ ] All custom logic has unit tests with edge cases\n- [ ] Zero amounts, max uint, empty arrays, self-transfers tested\n- [ ] Access control verified — unauthorized calls revert\n- [ ] Fuzz tests on all mathematical operations (minimum 1000 runs)\n- [ ] Fork tests for every external protocol integration\n- [ ] Invariant tests for stateful protocols (vaults, AMMs, lending)\n- [ ] Events verified with `expectEmit`\n- [ ] Gas snapshots taken with `forge snapshot` to catch regressions\n- [ ] Static analysis with `slither .` — no high/medium findings unaddressed\n- [ ] All tests pass: `forge test -vvv`\n"}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"f1328074-d001-408c-bdca-218a26851e2b","uuid":"89929870-3290-482e-abee-7af8ca25d070","timestamp":"2026-07-27T08:11:41.803Z","isSynthetic":true}

{"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-5","id":"msg_011CdSE8paCr1HfsJVFU9q3p","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_014oqWrWrozMomyJkPpLNMHk","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/Users/liana/Documents/prog/buidl-guidl/ethskills-evals/artifacts/testing-quiz-004/2026-07-27T081134Z-claude-with-skill-2/workspace/answer.md","content":"# Fork tests: one root cause, four symptoms\n\n## The root cause\n\n```solidity\nvm.createSelectFork(vm.envString(\"MAINNET_RPC_URL\"));\n```\n\nThe two-argument form takes a block number. You called the one-argument form, so the fork\nis pinned to **`latest`**. Nothing in your repo pins the chain state your tests run against.\n\nThat means the input to every one of these tests is \"whatever mainnet looked like the\nmoment CI happened to run.\" It is not a constant, it is not in git, and it is not reviewed.\nThe tests were never deterministic — they were *coincidentally* passing, and this morning\nthe coincidence ran out.\n\nEverything below falls out of that single line.\n\n## Why each symptom\n\n### 1. The sudden reds, with no code change\n\nThe tests assert on a Chainlink answer and on a pool's reserves. Both of those are live,\nconstantly-moving numbers on mainnet:\n\n- A Chainlink feed pushes a new answer on a deviation threshold (commonly 0.5%) or on its\n  heartbeat (commonly 1h). ETH/USD changes many times a day.\n- Uniswap reserves change on *every* swap, mint, and burn — many times per block.\n\nYour assertions compare those to constants that were baked in four months ago, presumably\nwith a tolerance band (`assertApproxEqRel`, or a `assertGt(reserves, X)` floor). Mainnet\ndrifted inside the band for four months, then this morning it drifted out. Nobody touched\nthe code because the code was never the variable. The chain was.\n\nThis is the classic signature: green for a long time, then red for all the\nmarket-data-dependent tests at once, on a commit that changed nothing.\n\n### 2. The flakiness on re-run\n\nTwo reasons, and both are consequences of `latest`:\n\n- **You're sitting on the boundary.** The value has just crossed the edge of your tolerance\n  band and is oscillating around it. Each CI run forks a different block, samples a\n  different value, and gets a different verdict. Same commit, different input, different\n  result. Re-running is a coin flip, which is exactly what you're observing.\n- **\"latest\" isn't even one answer.** Public RPC endpoints are load balancers in front of a\n  pool of nodes, and those nodes are not always on the same head. Two requests inside the\n  *same* test run can resolve `latest` to different blocks. So you can get an inconsistent\n  view of state within a single run, not just between runs.\n\n### 3. The steady slowdown\n\nFoundry caches fork RPC data on disk, keyed by chain and **block number**, under\n`~/.foundry/cache/rpc/<chain>/<block>/`. That cache is only reusable when you pin a block —\nforking at `latest` produces a new key every single run, so **every run is a 100% cache\nmiss.** Every account, every storage slot, every `eth_call` your tests touch is fetched cold\nover the network, every time.\n\nThat makes your fork suite network-bound rather than CPU-bound, and its runtime is\n`(number of RPC round trips) × (provider latency)`. Both of those terms have been creeping\nup over four months: the suite has more tests touching more slots, and free-tier provider\nlatency degrades as their load grows and as your usage climbs toward the limit. Once you\nstarted getting throttled (see below), Foundry's retry-and-backoff on rate-limited requests\nadded directly to wall-clock too.\n\nA pinned block turns the second run onward into a local disk read. The slowdown isn't a\nseparate problem; it's the cache you never got to use.\n\n### 4. The 429s\n\nSame mechanism. A cold-cache fork run against real protocols issues thousands of\n`eth_getStorageAt` / `eth_call` / `eth_getCode` requests. Multiply by every test, every job,\nevery PR, every re-run — and you have been paying that full cost on every single execution\nfor four months. Free tiers meter on requests or compute units per second and per month.\nYou grew into the ceiling and started getting throttled.\n\nAnd the 429s feed back into symptom 2: a throttled or failed fetch mid-run can surface as\nempty returndata or a spurious revert, so rate limiting is itself an *additional*\nindependent source of flakiness on top of the moving block.\n\n**The chain:** no pinned block → no cache reuse → every run refetches everything → request\nvolume grows past the free-tier limit → 429s and backoff → slower runs *and* more flakiness.\nMeanwhile the unpinned block means the assertions were sampling live market data the whole\ntime, which is what finally broke this morning.\n\n## The fix\n\nPin the block. That is the whole change.\n\n```solidity\ncontract PriceFeedForkTest is Test {\n    // Pinned fork block. This is a dependency version — treat bumping it like a\n    // dependency bump: deliberate, in its own PR, with expected values re-baselined.\n    uint256 constant FORK_BLOCK = 20_000_000;\n\n    function setUp() public {\n        vm.createSelectFork(vm.envString(\"MAINNET_RPC_URL\"), FORK_BLOCK);\n    }\n}\n```\n\nCleaner, using an alias so the URL lives in one place:\n\n```toml\n# foundry.toml\n[rpc_endpoints]\nmainnet = \"${MAINNET_RPC_URL}\"\n\n[profile.default]\n# Free tiers are well under Alchemy-ish defaults (330). Throttle client-side so the one\n# cold run that fills the cache doesn't trip the provider's limiter.\ncompute_units_per_second = 100\n```\n\n```solidity\nvm.createSelectFork(\"mainnet\", FORK_BLOCK);\n```\n\n### Then re-baseline the constants\n\nPinning makes the chain state a fixed input, so the expected values become *exactly*\nknowable. Read them once at `FORK_BLOCK` and assert on them exactly — drop the tolerance\nbands, they were only ever there to paper over the drift:\n\n```bash\ncast call 0x5f4eC3Df9cbd43714FE2740f5E3616155c5b8419 \"latestRoundData()\" \\\n  --rpc-url \"$MAINNET_RPC_URL\" --block 20000000\n```\n\n```solidity\n// ETH/USD at block 20_000_000\nassertEq(price, 3_431_12345678);\n```\n\nKeep `assertApproxEqAbs` / `assertApproxEqRel` only where *your own* math rounds, not to\nabsorb market movement. An exact assertion at a pinned block is a real regression detector;\na wide band around a moving number detects nothing until it detects everything at once,\nwhich is what happened this morning.\n\nTwo things pinning also fixes that you may not have connected yet: `block.timestamp` becomes\nfixed, so any deadline arithmetic stops drifting, and any Chainlink staleness guard\n(`require(block.timestamp - updatedAt < HEARTBEAT)`) stops being a lottery on how long ago\nthe feed last pushed.\n\n### Confirm the diagnosis in 30 seconds first\n\nBefore changing anything, add `console.log(block.number)` to `setUp` and run the suite\ntwice. Two different numbers is the whole bug, printed.\n\n## Does this work on a free-tier endpoint?\n\n**Mostly yes, with one real dependency you need to check: archive state access.**\n\nPinning to a block from last week or last month means asking the node for *state* at a\nhistorical block. A standard full node does not keep that. Geth's default retains state for\nroughly the last 128 blocks (~25 minutes) and prunes the rest; only an **archive node**\nserves `eth_getStorageAt` / `eth_call` / `eth_getBalance` / `eth_getCode` at arbitrary\nhistorical blocks. So:\n\n- If your free tier serves archive state → the fix works as written, and it will *reduce*\n  your request volume dramatically, because run two onward reads from the local cache.\n- If it doesn't → `vm.createSelectFork(url, FORK_BLOCK)` will fail on state reads, and\n  there is no way to pin around it. \"Pin to a very recent block\" is not a workaround; the\n  128-block window is about 25 minutes, far shorter than the gap between CI runs.\n\nFree tiers differ on this and providers change their plans, so don't take my word or a\nvendor page for it — probe your actual key.\n\n### How to tell, in one command\n\n```bash\ncast call 0x5f4eC3Df9cbd43714FE2740f5E3616155c5b8419 \"latestRoundData()(uint80,int256,uint256,uint256,uint80)\" \\\n  --rpc-url \"$MAINNET_RPC_URL\" --block 20000000\n```\n\n(Any historical block more than a few hours old works; that address is the mainnet Chainlink\nETH/USD feed.)\n\n- **Returns numbers** → you have archive access at that block. Done, ship the fix.\n- **`missing trie node` / `header not found` / `state not available`** → the node pruned\n  that state. Not an archive endpoint.\n- **HTTP 403, or an error naming your plan** → the provider has archive but gates it behind\n  a paid tier.\n- **HTTP 429** → inconclusive, you were just throttled. Wait and retry.\n\n**Important:** do not probe with `cast block 20000000`. Block headers and bodies are\nretained by full nodes, so that succeeds on a non-archive endpoint and will tell you the\nwrong thing. You have to request *state*.\n\n### If your free tier turns out not to serve archive\n\nIn order of how much I'd recommend them:\n\n1. **Commit the fork cache.** This is the strongest option for a free tier, because it\n   removes the RPC from CI entirely. Foundry's cache at\n   `~/.foundry/cache/rpc/mainnet/<FORK_BLOCK>/storage.json` is plain JSON. Have one person\n   with archive access generate it locally, commit it (or restore it in CI via\n   `actions/cache`, keyed on `FORK_BLOCK` so a bump invalidates it), and CI makes zero\n   network calls. Deterministic, fast, and free — no 429s possible. For a handful of\n   contracts it's typically tens to low hundreds of KB. Worth doing even if your endpoint\n   *does* have archive.\n2. **Get a second free key from a provider that does serve archive**, and point\n   `MAINNET_RPC_URL` at it. Several free tiers include archive data; verify with the probe\n   above rather than the marketing page.\n3. **Self-host or use a shared archive node.** Only worth it if you fork-test heavily.\n\nI would not suggest replacing the Chainlink and Uniswap calls with mocks here. That would\nmake the tests pass, but these are exactly the integration points fork tests exist to cover\n— mocking them deletes the coverage instead of fixing the flake.\n\n### Bumping the block later\n\nTreat `FORK_BLOCK` as a pinned dependency version. Bump it deliberately, in its own PR,\nre-baseline the expected values in the same PR, and let the diff show reviewers exactly how\nmuch mainnet moved. That way chain drift shows up as a reviewed change rather than as a red\nbuild on someone else's unrelated PR.\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":4797,"cache_read_input_tokens":27862,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":4797},"output_tokens":3,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"f1328074-d001-408c-bdca-218a26851e2b","uuid":"cd54102c-5469-46c2-8708-7f36b34b19d5","timestamp":"2026-07-27T08:14:31.746Z","request_id":"req_011CdSE8oTUkiD1LEsXDWvRV"}

You called the one-argument form, so the fork\nis pinned to **`latest`**. Nothing in your repo pins the chain state your tests run against.\n\nThat means the input to every one of these tests is \"whatever mainnet looked like the\nmoment CI happened to run.\" It is not a constant, it is not in git, and it is not reviewed.\nThe tests were never deterministic — they were *coincidentally* passing, and this morning\nthe coincidence ran out.\n\nEverything below falls out of that single line.\n\n## Why each symptom\n\n### 1. The sudden reds, with no code change\n\nThe tests assert on a Chainlink answer and on a pool's reserves. Both of those are live,\nconstantly-moving numbers on mainnet:\n\n- A Chainlink feed pushes a new answer on a deviation threshold (commonly 0.5%) or on its\n  heartbeat (commonly 1h). ETH/USD changes many times a day.\n- Uniswap reserves change on *every* swap, mint, and burn — many times per block.\n\nYour assertions compare those to constants that were baked in four months ago, presumably\nwith a tolerance band (`assertApproxEqRel`, or a `assertGt(reserves, X)` floor). Mainnet\ndrifted inside the band for four months, then this morning it drifted out. Nobody touched\nthe code because the code was never the variable. The chain was.\n\nThis is the classic signature: green for a long time, then red for all the\nmarket-data-dependent tests at once, on a commit that changed nothing.\n\n### 2. The flakiness on re-run\n\nTwo reasons, and both are consequences of `latest`:\n\n- **You're sitting on the boundary.** The value has just crossed the edge of your tolerance\n  band and is oscillating around it. Each CI run forks a different block, samples a\n  different value, and gets a different verdict. Same commit, different input, different\n  result. Re-running is a coin flip, which is exactly what you're observing.\n- **\"latest\" isn't even one answer.** Public RPC endpoints are load balancers in front of a\n  pool of nodes, and those nodes are not always on the same head. Two requests inside the\n  *same* test run can resolve `latest` to different blocks. So you can get an inconsistent\n  view of state within a single run, not just between runs.\n\n### 3. The steady slowdown\n\nFoundry caches fork RPC data on disk, keyed by chain and **block number**, under\n`~/.foundry/cache/rpc/<chain>/<block>/`. That cache is only reusable when you pin a block —\nforking at `latest` produces a new key every single run, so **every run is a 100% cache\nmiss.** Every account, every storage slot, every `eth_call` your tests touch is fetched cold\nover the network, every time.\n\nThat makes your fork suite network-bound rather than CPU-bound, and its runtime is\n`(number of RPC round trips) × (provider latency)`. Both of those terms have been creeping\nup over four months: the suite has more tests touching more slots, and free-tier provider\nlatency degrades as their load grows and as your usage climbs toward the limit. Once you\nstarted getting throttled (see below), Foundry's retry-and-backoff on rate-limited requests\nadded directly to wall-clock too.\n\nA pinned block turns the second run onward into a local disk read. The slowdown isn't a\nseparate problem; it's the cache you never got to use.\n\n### 4. The 429s\n\nSame mechanism. A cold-cache fork run against real protocols issues thousands of\n`eth_getStorageAt` / `eth_call` / `eth_getCode` requests. Multiply by every test, every job,\nevery PR, every re-run — and you have been paying that full cost on every single execution\nfor four months. Free tiers meter on requests or compute units per second and per month.\nYou grew into the ceiling and started getting throttled.\n\nAnd the 429s feed back into symptom 2: a throttled or failed fetch mid-run can surface as\nempty returndata or a spurious revert, so rate limiting is itself an *additional*\nindependent source of flakiness on top of the moving block.\n\n**The chain:** no pinned block → no cache reuse → every run refetches everything → request\nvolume grows past the free-tier limit → 429s and backoff → slower runs *and* more flakiness.\nMeanwhile the unpinned block means the assertions were sampling live market data the whole\ntime, which is what finally broke this morning.\n\n## The fix\n\nPin the block. That is the whole change.\n\n```solidity\ncontract PriceFeedForkTest is Test {\n    // Pinned fork block. This is a dependency version — treat bumping it like a\n    // dependency bump: deliberate, in its own PR, with expected values re-baselined.\n    uint256 constant FORK_BLOCK = 20_000_000;\n\n    function setUp() public {\n        vm.createSelectFork(vm.envString(\"MAINNET_RPC_URL\"), FORK_BLOCK);\n    }\n}\n```\n\nCleaner, using an alias so the URL lives in one place:\n\n```toml\n# foundry.toml\n[rpc_endpoints]\nmainnet = \"${MAINNET_RPC_URL}\"\n\n[profile.default]\n# Free tiers are well under Alchemy-ish defaults (330). Throttle client-side so the one\n# cold run that fills the cache doesn't trip the provider's limiter.\ncompute_units_per_second = 100\n```\n\n```solidity\nvm.createSelectFork(\"mainnet\", FORK_BLOCK);\n```\n\n### Then re-baseline the constants\n\nPinning makes the chain state a fixed input, so the expected values become *exactly*\nknowable. Read them once at `FORK_BLOCK` and assert on them exactly — drop the tolerance\nbands, they were only ever there to paper over the drift:\n\n```bash\ncast call 0x5f4eC3Df9cbd43714FE2740f5E3616155c5b8419 \"latestRoundData()\" \\\n  --rpc-url \"$MAINNET_RPC_URL\" --block 20000000\n```\n\n```solidity\n// ETH/USD at block 20_000_000\nassertEq(price, 3_431_12345678);\n```\n\nKeep `assertApproxEqAbs` / `assertApproxEqRel` only where *your own* math rounds, not to\nabsorb market movement. An exact assertion at a pinned block is a real regression detector;\na wide band around a moving number detects nothing until it detects everything at once,\nwhich is what happened this morning.\n\nTwo things pinning also fixes that you may not have connected yet: `block.timestamp` becomes\nfixed, so any deadline arithmetic stops drifting, and any Chainlink staleness guard\n(`require(block.timestamp - updatedAt < HEARTBEAT)`) stops being a lottery on how long ago\nthe feed last pushed.\n\n### Confirm the diagnosis in 30 seconds first\n\nBefore changing anything, add `console.log(block.number)` to `setUp` and run the suite\ntwice. Two different numbers is the whole bug, printed.\n\n## Does this work on a free-tier endpoint?\n\n**Mostly yes, with one real dependency you need to check: archive state access.**\n\nPinning to a block from last week or last month means asking the node for *state* at a\nhistorical block. A standard full node does not keep that. Geth's default retains state for\nroughly the last 128 blocks (~25 minutes) and prunes the rest; only an **archive node**\nserves `eth_getStorageAt` / `eth_call` / `eth_getBalance` / `eth_getCode` at arbitrary\nhistorical blocks. So:\n\n- If your free tier serves archive state → the fix works as written, and it will *reduce*\n  your request volume dramatically, because run two onward reads from the local cache.\n- If it doesn't → `vm.createSelectFork(url, FORK_BLOCK)` will fail on state reads, and\n  there is no way to pin around it. \"Pin to a very recent block\" is not a workaround; the\n  128-block window is about 25 minutes, far shorter than the gap between CI runs.\n\nFree tiers differ on this and providers change their plans, so don't take my word or a\nvendor page for it — probe your actual key.\n\n### How to tell, in one command\n\n```bash\ncast call 0x5f4eC3Df9cbd43714FE2740f5E3616155c5b8419 \"latestRoundData()(uint80,int256,uint256,uint256,uint80)\" \\\n  --rpc-url \"$MAINNET_RPC_URL\" --block 20000000\n```\n\n(Any historical block more than a few hours old works; that address is the mainnet Chainlink\nETH/USD feed.)\n\n- **Returns numbers** → you have archive access at that block. Done, ship the fix.\n- **`missing trie node` / `header not found` / `state not available`** → the node pruned\n  that state. Not an archive endpoint.\n- **HTTP 403, or an error naming your plan** → the provider has archive but gates it behind\n  a paid tier.\n- **HTTP 429** → inconclusive, you were just throttled. Wait and retry.\n\n**Important:** do not probe with `cast block 20000000`. Block headers and bodies are\nretained by full nodes, so that succeeds on a non-archive endpoint and will tell you the\nwrong thing. You have to request *state*.\n\n### If your free tier turns out not to serve archive\n\nIn order of how much I'd recommend them:\n\n1. **Commit the fork cache.** This is the strongest option for a free tier, because it\n   removes the RPC from CI entirely. Foundry's cache at\n   `~/.foundry/cache/rpc/mainnet/<FORK_BLOCK>/storage.json` is plain JSON. Have one person\n   with archive access generate it locally, commit it (or restore it in CI via\n   `actions/cache`, keyed on `FORK_BLOCK` so a bump invalidates it), and CI makes zero\n   network calls. Deterministic, fast, and free — no 429s possible. For a handful of\n   contracts it's typically tens to low hundreds of KB. Worth doing even if your endpoint\n   *does* have archive.\n2. **Get a second free key from a provider that does serve archive**, and point\n   `MAINNET_RPC_URL` at it. Several free tiers include archive data; verify with the probe\n   above rather than the marketing page.\n3. **Self-host or use a shared archive node.** Only worth it if you fork-test heavily.\n\nI would not suggest replacing the Chainlink and Uniswap calls with mocks here. That would\nmake the tests pass, but these are exactly the integration points fork tests exist to cover\n— mocking them deletes the coverage instead of fixing the flake.\n\n### Bumping the block later\n\nTreat `FORK_BLOCK` as a pinned dependency version. Bump it deliberately, in its own PR,\nre-baseline the expected values in the same PR, and let the diff show reviewers exactly how\nmuch mainnet moved. That way chain drift shows up as a reviewed change rather than as a red\nbuild on someone else's unrelated PR.\n","structuredPatch":[],"originalFile":null,"userModified":false}}
